b: Like the title says. I'm extremely ignorant about food. I grew with an almond mom, and I have eaten about every type of salad with every type of grain (never again, buckwheat, never again), but today I had to google what ravioli is.

All that to ask, please suggest dishes that I must make or eat at least once in my lifetime. I am learning to cook from scratch. There are so many recipes and dishes out there that I don't even know which ballpark to start in. I have no clue what I like or don't like, and may have never heard of the dish you suggest, but I'll be happy to try anything, easy or hard. Also, are there like overarching categories of other food, like soups, or is not that simple?

So far, I have made one pot chicken pesto pasta (which I loved so much that it started this journey) and pestoless variations thereof. I have eaten at restaurants before, but I can't tell you what, except that most of what I ate tasted amazing. I will eat anything (except peppers) that is not a salad!

(BONUS IF YOU GOT THIS FAR: when I had just moved out, for my first meal, I attempted to cook noodles. I did, however, try to cook them as you would cook rice, meaning putting them into cold water. By the time the water had boiled, they had disintegrated into the water and I was left with a literal fork fill of chewy noodles).
Edit: wow, I'm overwhelmed by the response! I am going to a dentist appointment soon, but when I'm back, I'll read through everything and make a list of all the suggestions!

Also, I apologize to the gluten intolerant and celiacs for the buckwheat slander. I know it's a great gluten free alternative, and works well as a part of a gluten free flour mix or a gluten free flour. However, in my opinion, it does NOT work well as the base for a salad, or as a "porridge", as the taste is so overwhelmingly strong (or maybe it was the way my mom prepared it).
